newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pioneer no comment on Ampol report.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pioneer no comment on Ampol report.

text.p: Pioneer International Ltd on Wednesday declined comment on a report it was considering the sale of its 50 percent stake in Australia's largest petroleum refiner and marketer, Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (Ampol).

"It is our company policy not comment on any possible acquisitions or divestments," Pioneer group corporate affairs manager Malcolm Lye told Reuters. The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Wednesday that Pioneer was considering a sale of Ampol due to concerns about its profitability.
Ampol is jointly owned by Pioneer and Caltex Australia Ltd.
Pioneer said on Friday there was a substantial reduction in first quarter profitability from Ampol, while the performance of its building business was flat.
Lye said the company continued to review all its operations in respect of providing an adequate return to shareholders.

The newspaper report quoted industry sources as saying the possibilities for the disposal of Ampol included sale through a float, a backdoor listing into Caltex, sale to Caltex's U.S. parent, Caltex Petroleum Corp, and a trade sale to another party. Caltex Petroleum is 50 percent owned by Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
Pioneer and Caltex Australia combined their petroleum assets last year in a A$3 billion merger.
Lye said there was still further scope for rationalisation through the closure of more petroleum service stations, as there were still too many service stations in Australia.
"As for corporate rationalisation, I can't comment," Lye said.
At 10.50 a.m. (2350 GMT), Pioneer shares were three cents up at A$3.38.
